title: Study in France: A Guide for Nepali Students
excerpt: Thinking about studying in France? Here is what Nepali students need to know about the French university system, low public tuition, Campus France, and the student visa process.

🇫🇷 Study in France — At a Glance
Public University FeesAmong the Lowest in Western Europe
Application PlatformCampus France (Études en France)

Why Nepali Students Are Looking at France

France is home to some of the world's oldest and most respected universities, and — unlike the UK, USA, or Australia — its public university system charges international students only a modest, government-set tuition fee rather than full market-rate fees. For Nepali students weighing cost against quality, that difference is significant: a genuine, globally recognized European degree at a fraction of what comparable programs cost elsewhere.

France also has two distinct higher education tracks worth understanding before you apply: public universities (open, moderate-fee, broad subject range) and the Grandes Écoles (selective, prestige-focused institutions for engineering, business, and public administration). Which track fits you depends on your academic background, budget, and career goals.

Understanding the French Higher Education System

Track 01
Public Universities
Open to any student meeting academic requirements. Government-regulated fees. Broad range of subjects across all levels — Licence (Bachelor's), Master's, Doctorat.
Track 02
Grandes Écoles
Highly selective specialist institutions for engineering, business, and public administration. Competitive entry, strong industry ties, and higher tuition than public universities.
Track 03
English-Taught Programs
A growing number of Master's programs — especially in business, engineering, and international relations — are taught fully in English, no French fluency required to start.

Tuition and Cost of Living

Public university tuition for international students in France has historically been set at a low, government-regulated rate — far below tuition at public universities in the UK, USA, Canada, or Australia. The exact figure is set by the French government and can change from year to year, so always confirm the current rate directly on Campus France or the specific university's admissions page before budgeting.

⚠️
Don't rely on last year's numbers Tuition rates, visa financial-proof thresholds, and work-hour limits are all set by French authorities and can change annually. Treat any specific figure you read online — including elsewhere on this site — as a starting estimate, and verify the current number on the official Campus France or France-Visas website before you apply.

Cost of living varies significantly by city — Paris is considerably more expensive than regional cities like Lyon, Lille, Toulouse, or Rennes, which offer a genuinely lower cost of living without compromising on education quality, and are increasingly popular with international students for exactly that reason.

The Student Visa Process

Nepali students planning to study in France for more than 90 days need a VLS-TS (Visa de Long Séjour valant Titre de Séjour) — a long-stay visa that also functions as your residence permit once validated after arrival. The process runs through the Études en France procedure on the Campus France platform, which is the mandatory first step for most degree-seeking applicants before a visa application can even be lodged.

  • Register on Campus France: Create your Études en France profile, apply to your chosen programs, and receive admission confirmation before booking a visa appointment.
  • Proof of financial resources: You'll need to show sufficient funds to cover your stay, at a level set periodically by French authorities — confirm the current requirement on France-Visas.
  • Proof of accommodation: A confirmed place to live in France, or a formal accommodation guarantee, is required as part of the visa file.
  • Health insurance: Proof of coverage valid in France is required before your visa is issued.
  • Visa interview: Conducted at the French visa application center — come prepared to explain your course choice and study plan clearly.

Working While You Study

International students on a valid French student visa are permitted to work part-time during their studies, up to a capped number of hours set by French labor law — enough to support living costs, though it should not be relied on as your primary funding source. Many students take up part-time roles in tutoring, hospitality, retail, or campus-based work. Always confirm the current legal work-hour cap for your visa type before committing to a part-time schedule.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to speak French to study in France?
Not necessarily. While most public university programs are taught in French and typically require proof of French proficiency (usually via TCF or DELF/DALF), a growing number of Master's programs — particularly in business, engineering, and international relations — are taught fully in English. Your language requirement depends entirely on which program and institution you choose.
What is Campus France and do I have to use it?
Campus France is the official French government platform for international students, and the Études en France procedure on it is the mandatory first step for most Nepali students applying to degree programs in France — you generally cannot apply for a long-stay student visa without having gone through it first.
Is France cheaper than the UK, USA, or Australia for international students?
Generally yes, at public universities — France's government-regulated tuition for international students is considerably lower than typical international tuition in the UK, USA, or Australia. Grandes Écoles and private institutions cost more, closer to what you'd pay elsewhere. Cost of living also varies a lot by city, with regional cities generally cheaper than Paris.
